summary: Tested new Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) SSO + page-level access control feature. Backend flows (login redirect, /auth/me, page-gated 401/403, sign-out) all verified via curl and confirmed correct. Frontend tested via Playwright with cookie injection (context.add_cookies DID work in this environment, contrary to main agent's earlier report - no SameSite/Secure issue found). Login page, unauthenticated flow, Super Admin full-app view, Pending Access screen, Limited-user nav filtering, Access Denied page, and Sign Out all work correctly and match spec. FOUND ONE CRITICAL BUG: the IT Access Management page's core Save function is completely broken.

critical.issue: Response excludes the user's `_id` field (projection is `{"_id": 0}`), but the frontend AccessManagementPage.jsx relies exclusively on `u._id` as the React key, the drafts-state key, the data-testid suffix, AND the user_id passed to `PUT /api/admin/users/{user_id}/access`. Since `_id` is always undefined client-side, ALL user rows share the literal key/testid 'undefined', causing: (1) a React 'duplicate key' console warning, (2) all rows' checkbox/draft state to be shared/aliased across different users (toggling one user's checkbox visually affects all rows), and (3) every 'Save Changes' click sends PUT /api/admin/users/undefined/access which the backend correctly 404s ('User not found'), so access changes can NEVER be saved through the UI at all.

ui_bugs.issue: All rows render with data-testid='access-management-row-undefined' / 'access-management-save-undefined' etc. instead of unique per-user ids, and Save Changes always fails with a 'User not found' toast (confirmed via UI click, network 404). Root cause is backend, see backend_issues.critical.

action_items: Fix GET /api/admin/users to include the user's _id in the response (e.g. project it back in as "id" or drop the exclusion, then update AccessManagementPage.jsx to use that field consistently) so Save Changes actually persists access grants/revocations.
After the fix, retest: toggle a checkbox for a non-admin test user, click Save, confirm the PUT succeeds (200) and the change persists on reload, and confirm each row/testid is now unique per user.
critical_code_review_comments: auth_service.py and the middleware design (PAGE_ROUTE_RULES, session-per-request re-lookup of role/allowed_pages for instant permission propagation) are well-architected and match the playbook description; no issues found there.

server.py admin_list_users() using find({}, {"_id": 0}) appears to be an oversight/copy-paste of a generic 'strip mongo objectid' pattern applied here even though _id is the actual usable string user_id (not an ObjectId) - it should be kept, not stripped.
Everything else (login redirect params, cookie flags, /auth/me never-401 contract, PAGE_ROUTE_RULES prefix matching) checked out correctly.
test_credentials: Used the 3 pre-made session cookies provided by main agent (super_admin, pending, limited-user) against vms_session cookie / auth_sessions & auth_users Mongo collections. /app/memory/test_credentials.md has no auth-specific entries (app previously had no end-user auth) - flagging that it should be updated with these 3 test accounts for future sessions, but did not modify it myself.
seed_data_creation: None created; reused main agent's 3 pre-existing test users/sessions. Restored newuser@rampgroup.co.in's allowed_pages back to [] (true pending state) after temporarily granting/testing it during the run, and restored rishabh's allowed_pages back to [] (role=super_admin already grants all pages regardless, unaffected by allowed_pages array). Final DB state: rishabh=super_admin, newuser=pending (0 pages), limiteduser=[bom_explorer, inventory] - matches original state described by main agent.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie injection via Playwright's page.context.add_cookies() WORKS FINE in this environment when domain is set to the exact hostname (no leading dot) with httpOnly/secure/sameSite=Lax matching the server's cookie flags - main agent's earlier report of it not working appears to have been a tool-specific issue in their own screenshot tool, not a real app bug or environment limitation. Next agent can reuse this technique directly. All 3 test sessions (super_admin, pending, limited) are still valid/reusable. The ONLY unresolved item is the /api/admin/users missing _id bug - once fixed, a quick re-run of the Access Management save flow (toggle checkbox -> Save -> reload -> verify persisted) is all that's needed to close this out.
rca_of_the_issue: GET /api/admin/users in server.py projects the Mongo find() with {"_id": 0}, stripping the document's _id (which in this schema IS the meaningful user_id string 'tid:oid', not a BSON ObjectId that would need hiding). AccessManagementPage.jsx then reads u._id (undefined) everywhere it needs a per-user identifier, including the PUT request path. Fix: remove the _id exclusion (or explicitly re-map it to a plain 'id' key) in the admin_list_users response, and have the frontend consistently use whichever field name is chosen.
